She states plainly that she intends to avoid surgery on principle — 'to keep me from the knife, which I don't believe in.' Follows a carnivore diet partly for pain and inflammation. Explicitly rejects the hormonal explanation for midlife weight gain.

notable.note: Two problems make this record unsafe to aggregate. The recording is truncated mid-presentation before price or outcome and continues in a second Drive file filed under the following day (1TY5F12DugGLjvAAOgFZUJzLxxMzLDuQ9), and it also shares its own file with an entirely separate sales call. One conversation therefore spans two files and two dates, while one file spans two conversations. Clinically it is one of the more concerning calls in the batch: a 50-year-old with a cervical disc problem, knees that prevent running, and a father disabled by eighteen spinal operations, who states outright that she refuses surgery on principle, was told that participants' shoulder and knee problems simply go away two to three months into the programme. She is also already performing loaded overhead kettlebell movements — halos and around-the-worlds — unsupervised, with a neck disc. Nobody asked whether any clinician had cleared it. Separately, she is a wellness practitioner herself and the rep pitched a business benefit to her looking the part, which is worth noting given the audience she serves.
